# Model and source

Ruppel 2017 contributes four models, all linked to this article:

* `Ruppel_2017_insulin` -- the population PK and PK-glucose infusion rate (PK-GIR)
  model for inhaled Technosphere insulin (TI) and subcutaneous regular human
  insulin (RHI).
* `Ruppel_2017_insulin_doseGIRAUC_TI`, `Ruppel_2017_insulin_doseGIRAUC_RHI` and
  `Ruppel_2017_insulin_doseGIRAUC_TIRHI` -- the three population dose-response
  (dose-GIRAUC) fits of Table 2 (TI alone, RHI alone, and both together with a
  common Hill coefficient). They are algebraic Emax models of the 0-20 h area
  under the insulin-induced GIR, fitted by the authors to GIR profiles simulated
  from the PK-GIR model.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ruppel_2017_insulin"))$reference`
* Description (PK-GIR): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Ruppel_2017_insulin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12189> (open access, with the NONMEM
  control streams of all three modelling steps as supplementary files)

# Population

The models come from study NCT01490762, a hyperinsulinemic euglycemic glucose
clamp crossover in 32 healthy volunteers at the Profil Institute (Chula Vista,
CA). Each subject received single doses of 10, 30, 60 and 80 U inhaled TI and
15 IU s.c. RHI on five occasions. One subject with occasionally very high
exposure was excluded, leaving 31 subjects (18 male, 13 female), aged 18-53
years and weighing 49-100 kg ('Study design and population' section). Insulin
was corrected for endogenous secretion with C-peptide and sampled for 3 h after
TI; GIR was recorded for 4 h after TI and 10 h after RHI.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Ruppel_2017_insulin")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry. "Stream" means the authors' NONMEM control stream in the supplement
(PK model code, PK-GIR model code, dose-GIRAUC model code).

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| `lka_sc` (ka,sc1, depot to transit) | 0.34 1/h | Table S1 |
| `lktr` (ka,sc2, transit to central) | 0.86 1/h | Table S1 |
| `lka_lung` (ka,TI,0 at 70 kg) | 1.64 1/h | Table S1 |
| `e_wt_ka_lung` (gamma_WT) | -1.7 | Table S1; footnote equation ka,TI = ka,TI,0 (WT/70)^gamma_WT |
| `lfdepot_lung` (F_TI relative to RHI) | 0.25 | Table S1 |
| `lvc` (V4) | 4.5 L | Table S1 |
| `lvp` (V5) | 56.4486 L, fixed | Table S1 (56.4, no CI); PK stream `$THETA 56.448600 FIX` |
| `lq` (Q) | 29.5602 L/h, fixed | Table S1 (29.6, no CI); PK stream `$THETA 29.560200 FIX` |
| `lkel` (ke0, elimination) | 8.55 1/h, fixed | Table S1; PK stream `$THETA 8.55 FIX ; Potocka 43.7/5.11` |
| `le0` (GIR0) | 2.7 mg/kg/min | Table 1 |
| `lemax` (GIRmax) | 11.9059 mg/kg/min, fixed | Table 1 (11.9, no CI); PK-GIR stream bounds `(11.905900 11.905900 11.905900)`; profiled, Supplementary Figure S2 |
| `lec50` (EC50) | 152 | Table 1 (labelled mU/L; see the effect-compartment note below) |
| `lhill` (gamma) | 1.8 | Table 1 |
| `lke0` (kin = kout) | 1.24 1/h | Table 1; one parameter `KEFF` in the PK-GIR stream |
| IIV ka,sc1 / ka,TI / F_TI / V4 / V5 | 48 / 21 / 29 / 22 / 102 % | Table S1 |
| IIV Emax / EC50 | 31 / 38 % | Table 1 |
| IOV F_TI / GIR0 | 30 / 61 % | Table S1 / Table 1; `$OMEGA BLOCK(1) SAME` in both streams |
| `propSd` (insulin) | 0.31 | Table S1 'p' |
| `addSd_GIR` | 2.1 mg/kg/min | Table 1 'sigma A' |
| Absorption and disposition ODEs | n/a | Figure 3; PK stream `$DES` |
| Effect compartment `d/dt(effect) = ke0 (central - effect)` | n/a | PK-GIR stream `DADT(6) = KEFF*(A(4)-A(6))`, `S6 = 1` |
| GIR = GIR0 + GIRmax Ce^gamma / (EC50^gamma + Ce^gamma) | n/a | Equation 2; PK-GIR stream `$ERROR` |
| Dose-GIRAUC Emax model | n/a | Equation 3; dose-GIRAUC stream `$PRED` |
| `lemax` (GIRAUC,max) | 14.287 g/kg, fixed | Equation 4 and Methods: 11.9 mg/kg/min x 1200 min = 14.3 g/kg |
| `led50` / `lhill` / `propSd`, TI fit | 249 U / 1.07 / 0.22 | Table 2, TI column (Fit 626954) |
| `led50` / `lhill` / `propSd`, RHI fit | 43 IU / 1.15 / 0.04 | Table 2, RHI column (Fit 629531) |
| `led50_lung` / `led50_sc` / `lhill` / `propSd`, common fit | 245 U / 48 IU / 1.08 / 0.21 | Table 2, TI/RHI column (Fit 47694) |
| IIV ED50 and gamma | 40 / 49 / 40, 45 % and 17 % | Table 2 |

# Typical-value PK and GIR profiles at the study doses

Doses are entered in mU (1 U = 1000 mU), the amount unit implied by the
insulin concentrations in mU/L and volumes in L. TI doses go to `depot_lung`
and RHI doses to `depot`. The model has two error endpoints (`Cc` and `GIR`),
so observation rows nominate one with `dvid`; both come back as columns.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Ruppel_2017_insulin")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

grid <- seq(0, 20, by = 1 / 60)
make_events <- function(arms, n_per_arm = 1L, wt = NULL) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
    ids <- (i - 1L) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm)
    w <- if (is.null(wt)) rep(70, n_per_arm) else wt[ids]
    dose <- data.frame(
      id = ids, time = 0, amt = arms$amt_mU[i], evid = 1L,
      cmt = arms$cmt[i], dvid = NA_integer_
    )
    obs <- expand.grid(time = grid, id = ids)
    obs <- data.frame(
      id = obs$id, time = obs$time, amt = 0, evid = 0L,
      cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L
    )
    bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
      left_join(data.frame(id = ids, WT = w), by = "id") |>
      mutate(OCC = 1L, treatment = arms$treatment[i])
  })) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

study_arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,    ~amt_mU, ~cmt,
  "TI 10 U",     10000,   "depot_lung",
  "RHI 15 IU",   15000,   "depot",
  "TI 30 U",     30000,   "depot_lung",
  "TI 60 U",     60000,   "depot_lung",
  "TI 80 U",     80000,   "depot_lung"
)
ev_typ <- make_events(study_arms)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame")
sim_typ$treatment <- factor(sim_typ$treatment, levels = study_arms$treatment)
```

```{r figure-s1-s3, fig.height = 6}
sim_typ |>
  filter(time <= 10) |>
  select(treatment, time, Cc, GIR) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, GIR)) |>
  mutate(name = ifelse(name == "Cc", "Insulin (mU/L)", "GIR (mg/kg/min)")) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
    caption = "Typical-value profiles; compare Supplementary Figures S1 (PK VPC)\nand S3 (PK-GIR VPC) of Ruppel 2017."
  )
```

The table compares the typical-value peaks with the observed-median peaks of the
prediction-corrected VPCs in Supplementary Figures S1 and S3, read by the
maintainers from the figures to the nearest grid fraction (approximate, so the
check is a coarse one that a wrong dose unit, volume or effect-compartment
scale would fail by a wide margin).

```{r vpc-peaks}
vpc_read <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,  ~cmax_vpc, ~girmax_vpc,
  "TI 10 U",   42,        5.5,
  "RHI 15 IU", 50,        12,
  "TI 30 U",   125,       9.8,
  "TI 60 U",   270,       12,
  "TI 80 U",   400,       14
)
peaks <- sim_typ |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(cmax = max(Cc), girmax = max(GIR), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(treatment = as.character(treatment)) |>
  left_join(vpc_read, by = "treatment")
stopifnot(
  all(abs(peaks$cmax / peaks$cmax_vpc - 1) < 0.35),
  all(abs(peaks$girmax / peaks$girmax_vpc - 1) < 0.35)
)
peaks |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  rename(
    "Treatment" = treatment,
    "Typical Cmax (mU/L)" = cmax,
    "VPC median peak, Fig. S1 (mU/L)" = cmax_vpc,
    "Typical peak GIR (mg/kg/min)" = girmax,
    "VPC median peak, Fig. S3 (mg/kg/min)" = girmax_vpc
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical-value peaks versus the approximate observed-median VPC peaks.")
```

## The effect compartment tracks the central amount

Table 1 labels EC50 in mU/L, but the authors' PK-GIR control stream integrates
`DADT(6) = KEFF*(A(4) - A(6))` with `S6 = 1`: the effect compartment follows the
central AMOUNT `A(4)` (mU) with a nominal 1-L scale, not the concentration
`A(4)/V4`. The packaged model follows the control stream. Driving the Emax
function with the concentration instead would give an RHI 15 IU peak GIR of
about 4 mg/kg/min, a third of the observed median peak in Figure S3B:

```{r effect-scale}
rhi15 <- sim_typ |> filter(treatment == "RHI 15 IU")
gir_amount <- max(rhi15$GIR)
gir_conc <- with(rhi15, max(e0 + emax * (effect / vc)^hill / (ec50^hill + (effect / vc)^hill)))
c(amount_driven = gir_amount, concentration_driven = gir_conc, vpc_observed_median = 12)
stopifnot(abs(gir_amount / 12 - 1) < 0.25, gir_conc < 0.5 * 12)
```

# Onset and duration of action (Figure 5 and Supplementary Table S2)

The authors compared 8 IU RHI with 40 U TI, a pair of doses with about the same
GIRAUC, through the cumulative insulin-induced GIRAUC normalised to its 0-20 h
total (Equation 6) and the times at which it reaches 10%, 50% and 90%. The
cumulative AUC is taken over GIR above the individual baseline, the quantity the
dose-GIRAUC stream fits (`AUCIPREDE0`); integrating total GIR instead pushes the
90% time past 1000 min for both insulins.

A virtual cohort of 200 subjects per arm is simulated with all random effects;
body weight is drawn log-normally around 72 kg and restricted (by redrawing) to
the study's 49-100 kg range, since the paper reports only the range.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2017)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2017)
draw_wt <- function(n) {
  w <- numeric(0)
  while (length(w) < n) {
    x <- exp(rnorm(n, log(72), 0.18))
    w <- c(w, x[x >= 49 & x <= 100])
  }
  w[seq_len(n)]
}
grid <- seq(0, 20, by = 5 / 60)
onset_arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,  ~amt_mU, ~cmt,
  "RHI 8 IU",  8000,    "depot",
  "TI 40 U",   40000,   "depot_lung"
)
n_onset <- 200L
ev_onset <- make_events(onset_arms, n_onset, wt = draw_wt(n_onset * nrow(onset_arms)))
sim_onset <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_onset, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame")

cum_times <- function(time_h, x) {
  cu <- cumsum(c(0, diff(time_h * 60) * (head(x, -1) + tail(x, -1)) / 2))
  tm <- time_h * 60
  c(t10 = tm[which(cu >= 0.1 * max(cu))[1]], t50 = tm[which(cu >= 0.5 * max(cu))[1]],
    t90 = tm[which(cu >= 0.9 * max(cu))[1]])
}
onset <- sim_onset |>
  group_by(id, treatment) |>
  summarise(tt = list(cum_times(time, GIR - e0)), .groups = "drop") |>
  unnest_wider(tt)
```

```{r figure-5}
sim_onset |>
  group_by(id, treatment) |>
  mutate(x = GIR - e0, cu = cumsum(c(0, diff(time) * (head(x, -1) + tail(x, -1)) / 2)), cu = cu / max(cu)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(id %in% c(1:31, n_onset + 1:31)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time * 60, cu, group = id, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("RHI 8 IU" = "magenta3", "TI 40 U" = "dodgerblue3")) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (min)", y = "Cumulative GIRAUC (fraction of 0-20 h)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Ruppel 2017 (31 virtual subjects per arm)."
  )
```

```{r table-s2}
published_s2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,  ~metric, ~mean, ~sd,
  "TI 40 U",   "t10",   35,    5,
  "TI 40 U",   "t50",   124,   25,
  "TI 40 U",   "t90",   386,   136,
  "RHI 8 IU",  "t10",   122,   23,
  "RHI 8 IU",  "t50",   296,   64,
  "RHI 8 IU",  "t90",   621,   152
)
sim_s2 <- onset |>
  pivot_longer(c(t10, t50, t90), names_to = "metric") |>
  group_by(treatment, metric) |>
  summarise(sim_mean = mean(value), sim_sd = sd(value), .groups = "drop")
cmp_s2 <- left_join(published_s2, sim_s2, by = c("treatment", "metric")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim_mean / mean - 1))
stopifnot(
  # T10 and T50 are set by absorption and the effect-compartment delay; a wrong
  # rate constant, route or effect scale moves them by tens of percent.
  all(abs(cmp_s2$pct_diff[cmp_s2$metric != "t90"]) < 15),
  # T90 sits in the long, right-skewed tail of the response (SD up to 40% of
  # the mean in the paper), so it gets a wider band.
  all(abs(cmp_s2$pct_diff[cmp_s2$metric == "t90"]) < 30)
)
cmp_s2 |>
  mutate(
    published = sprintf("%.0f +/- %.0f", mean, sd),
    simulated = sprintf("%.0f +/- %.0f", sim_mean, sim_sd),
    pct_diff = sprintf("%+.0f%%", pct_diff)
  ) |>
  select(treatment, metric, published, simulated, pct_diff) |>
  rename(
    "Treatment" = treatment, "Time to % of 0-20 h GIRAUC" = metric,
    "Published, min (mean +/- SD)" = published,
    "Simulated, min (mean +/- SD)" = simulated, "Difference" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Supplementary Table S2 of Ruppel 2017 versus the simulated cohort.")
```

# Dose-response (Figure 4 and Table 2)

The authors simulated GIR for 20 h with the PK-GIR model at doses up to 240 U TI
and 80 IU RHI, integrated the insulin-induced GIR, and fitted Equation 3 to the
resulting dose-GIRAUC pairs. Below, the same simulation is repeated with the
packaged PK-GIR model (100 virtual subjects per dose), and the median simulated
GIRAUC is set against the typical-value curves of the three packaged
dose-GIRAUC fits.

```{r dose-response-sim}
dr_arms <- bind_rows(
  tibble(dose = c(10, 30, 60, 80, 120, 180, 240), form = "TI", cmt = "depot_lung"),
  tibble(dose = c(4, 8, 15, 30, 45, 60, 80), form = "RHI", cmt = "depot")
) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(form, dose), amt_mU = 1000 * dose)
n_dr <- 100L
ev_dr <- make_events(dr_arms, n_dr, wt = draw_wt(n_dr * nrow(dr_arms)))
sim_dr <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_dr, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame")

auc_window <- function(time_h, x, upto) {
  keep <- time_h <= upto
  t <- time_h[keep] * 60
  y <- x[keep]
  sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2) / 1000 # mg/kg -> g/kg
}
girauc_sim <- sim_dr |>
  group_by(id, treatment) |>
  summarise(
    auc20 = auc_window(time, GIR - e0, 20),
    auc4 = auc_window(time, GIR - e0, 4),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(select(dr_arms, treatment, dose, form), by = "treatment") |>
  group_by(form, dose) |>
  summarise(med20 = median(auc20), mean20 = mean(auc20), med4 = median(auc4), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r dose-response-models}
dr_eval <- function(name, dose, form_ti = NULL) {
  m <- rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb(name))
  ev <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq_along(dose), evid = 0L, DOSE = dose)
  if (!is.null(form_ti)) ev$FORM_INSULIN_TI <- form_ti
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(m, ev, returnType = "data.frame")
  out$GIRAUC
}
dgrid <- seq(1, 240, by = 1)
curves <- bind_rows(
  tibble(form = "TI", fit = "TI fit", dose = dgrid,
         GIRAUC = dr_eval("Ruppel_2017_insulin_doseGIRAUC_TI", dgrid)),
  tibble(form = "RHI", fit = "RHI fit", dose = dgrid[dgrid <= 120],
         GIRAUC = dr_eval("Ruppel_2017_insulin_doseGIRAUC_RHI", dgrid[dgrid <= 120])),
  tibble(form = "TI", fit = "common fit", dose = dgrid,
         GIRAUC = dr_eval("Ruppel_2017_insulin_doseGIRAUC_TIRHI", dgrid, rep(1, length(dgrid)))),
  tibble(form = "RHI", fit = "common fit", dose = dgrid[dgrid <= 120],
         GIRAUC = dr_eval("Ruppel_2017_insulin_doseGIRAUC_TIRHI", dgrid[dgrid <= 120], rep(0, sum(dgrid <= 120))))
)
```

```{r figure-4a}
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = curves, aes(dose, GIRAUC, colour = form, linetype = fit)) +
  geom_point(data = girauc_sim, aes(dose, med20, colour = form), size = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(RHI = "magenta3", TI = "dodgerblue3")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("TI fit" = "solid", "RHI fit" = "solid", "common fit" = "dashed")) +
  labs(
    x = "Dose (U TI or IU RHI)", y = "GIRAUC, 0-20 h (g/kg)", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 4a of Ruppel 2017. Lines: typical-value dose-GIRAUC fits (Table 2);",
      "points: median 0-20 h GIRAUC simulated from the PK-GIR model.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  )
```

```{r dose-response-check}
dr_check <- girauc_sim |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(model = if (form == "TI") {
    dr_eval("Ruppel_2017_insulin_doseGIRAUC_TI", dose)
  } else {
    dr_eval("Ruppel_2017_insulin_doseGIRAUC_RHI", dose)
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(ratio = med20 / model)
stopifnot(
  # The two packaged layers must agree on the dose-response they share. A wrong
  # ED50 (e.g. the TI and RHI values swapped) or a GIRAUC,max off by the
  # minutes-to-hours factor moves this ratio far outside the band.
  abs(median(dr_check$ratio) - 1) < 0.15,
  # Envelope on a robust quantile: the per-dose medians of 100 subjects are
  # noisy at the lowest doses, where GIRAUC is small and right-skewed.
  quantile(abs(dr_check$ratio - 1), 0.75) < 0.3
)
dr_check |>
  mutate(across(c(med20, mean20, model, ratio), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  select(form, dose, med20, mean20, model, ratio) |>
  rename(
    "Insulin" = form, "Dose (U / IU)" = dose,
    "Simulated median GIRAUC (g/kg)" = med20, "Simulated mean GIRAUC (g/kg)" = mean20,
    "Dose-GIRAUC fit, typical (g/kg)" = model, "Median / fit" = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "PK-GIR simulation versus the formulation-specific dose-GIRAUC fits.")
```

For RHI the two layers agree to within about 10% from 8 IU upward; at 4 IU the
simulated GIRAUC is small and right-skewed, so its median falls below the
typical-value curve. For TI the PK-GIR simulation rises more steeply than the
fitted Emax curve at low doses and flattens faster above about 120 U, because the
high, sharp TI peaks saturate the GIR Emax function; the TI dose-GIRAUC fit
absorbs this shape misfit in its larger proportional error (22% against 4% for
RHI, Table 2). The simulated 4-h half-maximal doses below (about 22 IU RHI and
29 U TI) are close to the published 20 IU and 35 U.

## Equivalent doses

The common fit gives the paper's dose-conversion factor, the ED50 ratio
(Equation 5):

```{r conversion}
common <- readModelDb("Ruppel_2017_insulin_doseGIRAUC_TIRHI")
ini_common <- rxode2::rxode(common)$iniDf
ed50_ratio <- exp(ini_common$est[ini_common$name == "led50_lung"]) /
  exp(ini_common$est[ini_common$name == "led50_sc"])
ed50_ratio
stopifnot(abs(ed50_ratio - 5.1) < 0.05)
```

## A 4-h integration window

Figure 4b shows that truncating the integral at 4 h produces an apparent
saturation, with half-maximal doses of 20 IU RHI and 35 U TI. With the maximum
4-h GIRAUC fixed at GIRmax x 240 min = 2.86 g/kg, the dose at which the median
simulated 4-h GIRAUC reaches half of it is interpolated below:

```{r figure-4b}
half4 <- 11.9059 * 240 / 1000 / 2
ed50_4h <- girauc_sim |>
  group_by(form) |>
  summarise(ed50_4h = approx(med4, dose, xout = half4)$y, .groups = "drop")
ed50_4h
stopifnot(
  abs(ed50_4h$ed50_4h[ed50_4h$form == "RHI"] / 20 - 1) < 0.3,
  abs(ed50_4h$ed50_4h[ed50_4h$form == "TI"] / 35 - 1) < 0.3
)
```

# PKNCA

The paper reports no NCA. Insulin exposure from the stochastic simulation at the
five study doses is summarised with PKNCA for reference, and a typical-value
identity checks the disposition: the 0-72 h AUC times the apparent clearance
`kel * V4` must equal the bioavailable dose.

```{r pknca}
ev_nca <- make_events(study_arms, 100L, wt = draw_wt(100L * nrow(study_arms)))
sim_nca <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_nca, keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  ev_nca |> filter(evid == 1) |> select(id, time, amt, treatment),
  amt ~ time | treatment + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 20, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)
```

```{r auc-identity}
# Integrate to 72 h: the slow s.c. absorption (ka,sc1 = 0.34 1/h) leaves about
# 1% of the RHI AUC beyond 20 h.
grid <- seq(0, 72, by = 1 / 60)
sim_long <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, make_events(study_arms), keep = "treatment", returnType = "data.frame")
sim_long$treatment <- factor(sim_long$treatment, levels = study_arms$treatment)
typ_auc <- sim_long |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2),
    cl = kel[1] * vc[1], f = fdepot_lung[1], .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(study_arms |> mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, levels = treatment)), by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(
    f_eff = ifelse(cmt == "depot_lung", f, 1),
    ratio = auc * cl / (f_eff * amt_mU)
  )
typ_auc |> select(treatment, auc, ratio)
stopifnot(all(abs(typ_auc$ratio - 1) < 0.002))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Effect compartment scale.** Table 1 gives EC50 in mU/L, but the PK-GIR
  control stream drives the effect compartment with the central amount (`A(4)`,
  mU) and fixes its scale to 1 (`S6 = 1`). The packaged model follows the code;
  the concentration-driven alternative under-predicts the observed GIR peaks by
  about two thirds (see above). EC50 therefore has amount units (mU, nominally
  per 1 L), and it interacts with the individual central volume.
- **Dose units.** Doses are in mU of labelled units (1 U = 1000 mU): TI doses in
  Technosphere units, RHI doses in international units. TI bioavailability is
  relative to RHI, so the volumes and clearance are apparent values relative to
  RHI bioavailability (Table S1 footnote). The authors estimate the absolute TI
  bioavailability at 12-13% using an RHI bioavailability of 53% from Potocka
  2010.
- **Variance scale.** The tables print each random-effect magnitude as a
  percentage. The packaged variances use omega^2 = (percent/100)^2 (log-scale
  SD). The Table S1 V5 row, '102 (76-123)', decides it: the interval is
  symmetric on the variance scale under that reading (midpoint 1.045 against
  1.040), and not under omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2) (midpoint 0.689 against 0.713,
  outside rounding). The same reading is applied to every table.
- **Fixed values from the code.** V5, Q and GIRmax are printed without
  confidence intervals; the control streams show them fixed (V5 and Q from
  earlier fits, GIRmax by likelihood profiling, Supplementary Figure S2). The
  code's unrounded values are used. The elimination rate constant (8.55 1/h) is
  fixed from Potocka 2010 as 43.7/5.11.
- **Occasions.** The PK stream indexes the TI bioavailability IOV by four TI
  occasions (`OCC` 3-6) and the PK-GIR stream indexes the GIR-baseline IOV by
  five visits (`VISIT` 3-7). The packaged model indexes both by one `OCC = 1-5`
  column; the extra bioavailability slot is inert on the RHI occasion because
  only TI carries a bioavailability. The GIR baseline has IOV but no IIV (its
  IIV is fixed to 0 in the stream).
- **Logit bioavailability.** The PK stream passes F_TI through
  `PHI = LOG(FTI/(1-FTI))`, `F3 = EXP(PHI)/(1+EXP(PHI))`, which returns F_TI
  unchanged; the packaged model applies F_TI directly. (In NONMEM an individual
  F_TI above 1 would make `PHI` undefined; with the published variances this
  happens for about 1 in 2000 occasions.)
- **Dose-GIRAUC maximum.** In the dose-GIRAUC fits GIRAUC,max is not a
  parameter but each subject's GIRmax times 1200 min, entered as a data column.
  The packaged dose-GIRAUC models carry it as a fixed typical value,
  11.9059 x 1.2 = 14.287 g/kg (the paper rounds to 14.3), with a fixed random
  effect equal to the PK-GIR Emax variability (31%) so that simulations
  reproduce the between-subject spread the fits conditioned on. The caption
  of Figure 4 quotes a maximum of 13.8 g/kg, which the paper does not derive.
- **Dose-GIRAUC output.** `GIRAUC` is the 0-20 h integral of GIR above the
  individual baseline (the dose-GIRAUC stream's dependent variable is
  `AUCIPREDE0`), in g/kg. It is a paper-specific output name, not a registered
  canonical endpoint.
- **Virtual cohort.** The paper reports only the weight range (49-100 kg), so
  weights are drawn log-normally around 72 kg and redrawn outside the range.
  Each simulated subject receives one treatment on occasion 1.
- **VPC comparison.** The observed-median peaks of Supplementary Figures S1 and
  S3 were read approximately from the figures by the maintainers; they support a
  coarse check only.
- **Errata.** No correction notice for this article was found in Europe PMC as
  of 2026-11-25.
